unmapped_findings: [Alloy/study-level, applicable to this sample's material but not a value specific to 950 °C/10 s^-1] The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1, obtained from k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690 (Fig. 4); it is only an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines are not parallel (b0032, b0034, b0085).

[Alloy/study-level] Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

[Alloy/study-level trend] The paper states that fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C / 1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086); this sample (950 °C/10 s^-1) falls in the low-T/high-ε̇ corner of the map, outside this optimum window.

[High strain rate group, includes this sample] At ε̇ = 10 s^-1 the peak stress decreases by 73% over 900–1150 °C, compared with an 82% reduction at 0.01 s^-1 (b0024); the specific peak stress at 950 °C/10 s^-1 is not tabulated in the paper.

No optical micrograph and no direct measured property value is reported specifically at 950 °C and 10 s^-1. The nearest reported micrograph is Fig. 9(d), which is 950 °C at 1 s^-1 (a different sample), showing banded/elongated structure with numerous large elongated remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains (b0063, figure_009).

DRX state diagram (Fig. 7, b0058) defines three zones in the lnZ–strain space: A = work hardening, B = partial DRX, C = complete DRX; both critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs increase with increasing lnZ (increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature), i.e. starting and completing DRX becomes more difficult.
